content: 1. Penicillins exhibit bactericidal activity. When used concurrently with tetracyclines, monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins, as tetracyclines may interfere with their bactericidal action. 2. Ascorbic acid can reduce the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 3. Products containing multivalent cations may impair the absorption of tetracyclines, potentially reducing their efficacy. Dosing of tetracyclines should be separated from these products to avoid interaction. 4. Aspirin combined with citric acid and sodium bicarbonate can decrease the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is relevant only for oral formulations of both agents. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. 5. Omadacycline can enhance the effects of atracurium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Bexarotene may increase the toxicity of omadacycline through an unknown mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Concurrent use of oral retinoids with tetracyclines may elevate the risk of pseudotumor cerebri or intracranial hypertension. Monitor patients closely. 8. Bismuth subgallate reduces the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 9. Omadacycline increases the effects of cisatracurium through pharmacodynamic synergism, posing a risk of respiratory depression. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Citric acid combined with sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are advised. 11. Cholera vaccine efficacy may be reduced by omadacycline due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration of cholera vaccine with systemic antibiotics, as these agents may act against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 12. Cholestyramine decreases the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 13. Chromium reduces the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are necessary. 14. Isotretinoin increases the toxicity of omadacycline through an unknown mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Concurrent use of oral retinoids with tetracyclines may increase the risk of pseudotumor cerebri or intracranial hypertension. Monitor patients closely. 15. Magnesium chloride decreases the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 16. Magnesium citrate reduces the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. 17. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 18. Magnesium oxide reduces the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are necessary. 19. Iron-containing products, such as ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, ferrous sulfate, ferric citrate, ferric gluconate, ferric maltol, ferric pyrophosphate dialysate, and iron sucrose, decrease the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions apply only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored, and dosing of tetracyclines should be separated from these products. 20. Folic acid reduces the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are advised. 21. Iodine decreases the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 22. Copper reduces the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are necessary. 23. Cyanocobalamin decreases the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 24. Iron/folic acid/vitamin/mineral combinations reduce the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended.
